announcements.content:
OFFICIAL STATEMENT — HIGH LINE RACING NETWORK

Effective immediately, Matthew Brown is no longer eligible to participate in any High Line Racing Network league or hosted race.

This decision follows his actions in tonight’s Carson Hocevar $10,000 race. While a lap down, Brown drove through the grass and back onto the racing surface, wrecking multiple competitors and compromising their chances at the $10,000 prize. Brown also admitted that he wrecked them intentionally.

This was more than a racing mistake. Intentionally ruining other competitors’ races shows a disregard for their time, effort, and opportunity to compete. That behavior is unacceptable and has no place in our fields.

As we have stated before, we will protect the integrity of our races. We must be able to trust every driver on our grid to compete with respect and sportsmanship. Brown’s actions and admission have broken that trust.

HLRN stands behind the drivers who race fairly and respect their fellow competitors. We will uphold those standards through our decisions and our actions.
Switching to Dega after a bunch of request

🏁 **HLRN RACE CONTROL — POST-RACE BULLETIN** 🏁

Following our post-race review of last night’s event, Race Control determined that **Matthew Brown was found at fault for two separate incidents and should have received a Green Flag Pass-Through Penalty.**

That penalty was missed during the race.

We’ve said from the beginning that Race Control won’t be perfect. We make decisions in real time while reviewing incidents, tracking penalties, communicating with drivers, and managing the race. Last night brought more cautions and incidents than anticipated, and unfortunately, this was an oversight on our part.

Race Control discussed the situation after the race and takes responsibility for the missed penalty.

Fortunately, it does not appear that the missed Green Flag Pass-Through had a significant impact on the final race results. However, **that does not make the mistake acceptable or something we simply brush aside.** We take the consistency and integrity of HLRN officiating seriously, and we are already working on measures to help prevent this type of oversight in the future.

**We also need our drivers to help us catch something if it doesn’t look right.**

For example, if you recognize that a driver has received an **EOL when their accumulated at-fault incidents should have resulted in a Green Flag Pass-Through**, respectfully bring it to Race Control’s attention. You are not challenging Race Control by doing so—you are giving us an opportunity to double-check the situation and correct a potential mistake **while we still have the opportunity to enforce the proper penalty during the race.**

Race Control will always make the final determination, but if something appears to have been missed, **speak up respectfully. We would rather verify it than unknowingly allow an incorrect penalty to stand.**

Our commitment is simple: **call the race as fairly and consistently as possible, enforce the rules equally, and protect the competitive integrity of HLRN.** When we get something wrong, we’ll own it, address it, and work to make sure we’re better the next time.

We expect accountability from our drivers, and **Race Control should be held to that same standard.**

🏁 **HLRN Race Control**
*If you’re not on the High Line, you’re already behind!*

🚨 HLRN Monday Night League, Season 2 Information 🚨

@everyone 

Our Season 2 Monday Night League officially kicks off Monday, August 10th!

As of today, drivers are free to recruit teammates and form race teams (C Class License at minimum). Once your team has been established, please designate a Team Captain. **We will have a limit of 10 teams**

**Team Captains:**
Please send me a private DM with the following:

* Team Name
* Complete Driver Roster
* Driver Numbers

*Teams are restricted to 5 drivers for Monday League* 4 Driver teams are allowed

**Number Assignments**

Please head over to the Number Assignments channel in our Monday League tab and report an available number to your team captain.

Any numbers that are already filled are reserved for our Sunday League drivers and will remain locked, regardless of whether that driver competes on Monday nights. Our goal is for drivers to build an identity within HLRN by keeping the same number for years to come.

If you’re a new Monday-only driver, choose an available number and report it to your Team Captain. Number assignments will be awarded on a first-come, first-served basis once Team Captains submit their official roster and team name.  (ANY NUMBER MARKED FILL IN EXCEPT FOR THE #6 IS STILL AVAILABLE)

**Schedule**

The official Season 2 schedule has been posted! All races will be broadcast live on RSI Broadcasting via YouTube.

**League Entry Fee**

The league entry fee is $40 per driver and must be paid by Wednesday, August 5th.

Payments must be sent via Venmo to @tommylrogers.

Team Captains are responsible for making sure every driver on their roster has paid by the deadline.

Failure to pay by August 5th will result in forfeiture of your assigned car number and roster spot.

We will only accept payment through Venmo. If you don’t have a Venmo account, find a teammate, friend, or family member who can submit your payment, then reimburse them however you’d like.

Let’s get these teams built and get ready for another great season. See you boys on August 10th!
